title: Practice 8: Setting out: пойти, поехать — and сходить, съездить

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Что ты забыл на чердаке? Какого лешего тебя туда ___ (понести — to carry off (on foot))?
exercises.why: **понесло** is the past tense (neuter) of **понести** (to carry (for a while) — the perfective of **нести**, «set out». past: он понёс · она понесла́ · оно понесло́ · они понесли́. — Wiktionary, «понести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: What did you forget in the attic? What the hell made you go there?
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: Если ___ (поехать — to set off (by vehicle)) по кольцевой дороге, то окажешься там быстрее.
exercises.why: **поедешь** is the future tense (2nd person singular) of **поехать** (to go (in a conveyance or on horseback)) — the perfective of **ехать**, «set out». future: я пое́ду · ты пое́дешь · он пое́дет · мы пое́дем · вы пое́дете · они пое́дут. — Wiktionary, «поехать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The future perfective (поеду, поедешь) belongs to the 1st -е- type of conjugation.» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «ехать — ездить: perfective поехать · «for a while» поездить · «round trip» съездить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Мы поездили по городу и поехали домой.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: If you take the ring road, you'll get there faster.
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.why: **повело** is the past tense (neuter) of **повести** (to lead, to conduct, to direct, to drive) — the perfective of **вести**, «set out». past: он повёл · она повела́ · оно повело́ · они повели́. — Wiktionary, «повести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: The driver skidded on a slippery road and collided with the crash barrier.
exercises.context: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). (DLI, Lesson 54)

exercises.q: Хотя Арине только шестнадцать, она хорошо ___ (сходить — to go and come back (on foot)) за взрослую девушку.
exercises.why: **сходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **сходить** (to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off) — the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back. present: я схожу́ · ты схо́дишь · он схо́дит · мы схо́дим · вы схо́дите · они схо́дят. — Wiktionary, «сходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «b) Prefix "с-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "с-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — ходить, ездить, летать — forms perfective verbs: сходить, съездить, слетать. These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  «идти — ходить: perfective пойти · «for a while» походить · «round trip» сходить.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Он сходил к другу.» (He went to a friend's place (and has returned; see prefixed perfective forms of motion verbs below).) — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0). «Мне надо сходить на почту за письмами.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Although Arina is 16 years old, she imitates an adult woman well.
exercises.context: However, prefixes "по-" and "с-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs. (DLI, Lesson 63)

exercises.q: Что ж, вы ___ (полететь — to fly off) бы?
exercises.why: **полетели** is the past tense (plural) of **полететь** (to fly, to be flying) — the perfective of **лететь**, «set out». past: он полете́л · она полете́ла · оно полете́ло · они полете́ли. — Wiktionary, «полететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "по" to the actual function verbs ("идти", "ехать", etc.). The perfective verbs пойти and поехать denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").» — DLI, Lesson 54.  «The perfective verb полететь (like пойти and поехать) denotes single action with the emphasis on the completed start. The past perfective (полетел, -ла, -ло, -ли) is formed in a regular way. The future perfective (полечу, полетишь) belongs to the 2nd (-и-) type of conjugation. The consonant "т" changes into "ч" in the first person singular only.» — DLI, Lesson 55.  «The addition of the prefix по- to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «лететь — летать: perfective полететь · «for a while» полетать · «round trip» слетать.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  Compare: «Полковник полетел в Вашингтон.» (The Colonel flew to Washington. (single action; completed start)) — DLI, Lesson 55. «Завтра я полечу на фронт.» (Tomorrow I'll fly to the front. (single action)) — DLI, Lesson 55.  ·  From Фёдор Достоевский, «Преступление и наказание».
